rows.ARS:
Medium pink Shrub.
Registration name: Belinda's Dream (Shrub, Basye, 1988)
Exhibition name: Belinda's Dream
rows.Origin: Bred by Dr. Robert E. Basye (United States, 1988).
rows.Bloom: Pink. Moderate, fruity, raspberry fragrance. 45 to 100 petals. Average diameter 4". Medium-large, very full (41+ petals) bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit: Medium, arching, bushy, lax. Glossy, dark green foliage.
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7a through 11. Can be used for cut flower, garden or landscape. Heat tolerant. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant.
rows.Notes:
Dr. Bayse named this rose after a friend’s daughter in Caldwell, Texas.

In his garden in Tyler, Texas, Mark Chamblee, of Chamblee's Rose Nursery, grew 'Belinda's Dream', 'Marie Daly', 'Marie Pavie', 'Livin' Easy', 'Easy Going', 'Knockout', and 'Mermaid'. Mark liked these varieties because "they have great hardiness and disease resistance, they are low maintenance and are very free blooming."
